U.S. Africa Command (USAFRICOM) is seeking interested commercial vendors for targeted Industry Sessions to be held in Tunis, Tunisia. While the main conference has its own agenda, these specific Industry Sessions are a separate, USAFRICOM-hosted opportunity focused on showcasing military technologies, supplies or services available for acquisition by African Partner nations. Selected vendors will be provided with a dedicated space to present their capabilities. They will also be invited to attend the main conference sessions as observers. The logistical details for this specific USAFRICOM Industry Day session are as follows: � Date and Time: 2 February to 4 February 2027 from 08:00 to 17:00 local time � Location: Event location will be provided to selected vendors along with various lobby and foyer spaces adjacent to the conference plenary space. � Provided Space: Open Space for models, displays, and demonstrations. � Permitted Materials: Non-USG provided technologies, super intelligence (AI), and equipment such as drones and unattended sensors, marketing brochures, and operational product samples. Digital presentations on laptops and monitors are permitted. Primary Areas of Interest The U.S. Government is interested in vendors with capabilities in the following fields, though all submissions will be considered: � Geospatial: Drones (UAV/UAS), Commercial GEOINT, Remote Sensing, and Tracking Systems � Command and Control: C4ISR and Airborne C2 Systems � Consulting & Administrative: Systems Integration, Enterprise Architecture, and Acquisition Management � Drones (UAV/UAS) and Counter-UAS: Platforms as well as Counter-UAS and IED detection technologies � Big Data & Software: Intelligence Analytics, Social Media Analysis, Open-Source Intelligence, and Artificial Intelligence � Cyber: Cyber/Info Security, Intrusion Detection, and Vulnerability/Threat Assessment Submission Requirements for Capability Statement Any commercial vendor may submit a Capability Statement and will be considered for participation. The U.S. Government has final approval of all exhibitor selections to ensure strategic objectives for the conference are met. description: Obiectul contractului îl reprezintă prestarea de servicii de dezvoltare, integrare, testare, punere în funcțiune și pilotare a unui ansamblu de 7 soluții digitale. Soluțiile sunt destinate Comunei Căpâlnița și Comunei Lueta, în cadrul proiectului „Dezvoltarea digitală în cadrul parteneriatului între Comuna Căpâlnița și Comuna Lueta”. Proiectul este finanțat prin Programul „Regiunea Centru” 2021–2027, Prioritatea 2 „O regiune digitală”, Intervenția 2.1.1. Cele 7 soluții sunt: -digitalizarea serviciilor publice oferite de UAT; -comunicarea bidirecțională cu cetățenii; -optimizarea fluxurilor interne ale primăriei; -platforma de educare și conștientizare; -asistentul virtual (chatbot) bazat pe inteligență artificială; -sistemul de raportare și analiză (Business Intelligence); -modulul de monitorizare și optimizare a consumului energetic. Soluțiile vor fi livrate ca ecosistem digital integrat, pe o arhitectură modulară comună, cu izolarea datelor fiecărui UAT. Interfețele destinate cetățenilor vor fi accesibile (WCAG 2.1, nivel minim AA) și bilingve (română și maghiară). Obiectivul general al proiectului îl reprezintă modernizarea serviciilor publice furnizate de administrațiile locale ale Comunei Căpâlnița și Comunei Lueta, prin implementarea unui ansamblu de 7 soluții digitale integrate, în vederea digitalizării proceselor administrative, a îmbunătățirii comunicării cu cetățenii și mediul de afaceri și a creșterii eficienței interne a celor două primării. Obiective specifice - OBS1 — Dezvoltarea și implementarea celor 7 soluții digitale integrate, ca ansamblu funcțional, pilotat și recepționat în ambele UAT-uri; - OBS2 — Digitalizarea proceselor administrative prin fluxuri automatizate (minimum 3 fluxuri de lucru administrative automatizate); - OBS3 — Implicarea cetățenilor prin bugetare participativă (platformă care permite implicarea a minimum 538 de cetățeni, cumulat pe durata proiectului); - OBS4 — Promovarea accesibilității și educației digitale (minimum 700 de utilizatori unici; minimum 2 sesiuni de instruire pentru cetățeni și reprezentanți ai companiilor, pentru a facilita utilizarea soluțiilor digitale); - OBS5 — Reducerea timpilor de răspuns administrativ (de la ~7 zile la 48 de ore); - OBS6 — Creșterea eficienței energetice și a sustenabilității, prin modulul de monitorizare și optimizare a consumului energetic. Număr de zile până la care se pot solicita clarificări înainte de data-limită de depunere a ofertelor: 15 zile. În măsura în care solicitările de clarificări au fost adresate în termenul precizat în documentație, termenul de răspuns al autorității contractante este de 10 zile înainte de data-limită de depunere a ofertelor. Orice solicitare de clarificări trebuie transmisă în SEAP (http://sicap-prod.e-licitatie.ro/pub).

SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company�s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click �My Profile�, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand �E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)�, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click �Send.� For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. title: NGA HRM-II RFP
description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Registration MUST contain the appropriate North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541612 � Human Resources Consulting Services Size Standard $29M. ***Amendment 0003 � Solicitation Update*** The Government is issuing Amendment 0003 to Solicitation No. HM047626R0018 for HRM II. The purpose of this amendment is to revise solicitation instructions and extend key solicitation dates. Summary of Changes: 1. This amendment incorporates Attachment 16, Supplemental Section 4 � Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors, Revision 3, and updates the following sections: - Section 4.4(A) � General Proposal Instructions - Section 4.5 � Information to Offerors - Section 4.7(F) � Solicitation Question and Answer Period - Section 4.7(G) � Proposal Submission and Due Date - Section 4.10(C) � Volume 2 � Factor 1: Technical/Management Approach Subfactors 2. Revised Dates: - Question Submission Due Date:19 October 2026, 3:00 PM Eastern Time - Proposal Submission Due Date:18 November 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time 3. Questions and Answers: The Government will provide responses to industry questions in Solicitation Amendment 0004. 4. Important Note: Except as expressly amended herein, all other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged and in full force and effect. ***Amendment 0002 � Solicitation Access Update and Reopening of Question Period*** The Government is issuing Amendment 0002 to Solicitation No. HM047626R0018 for HRM II dated 20261008. 1. The purpose of this amendment is to ensure all interested parties have a fair opportunity to review the requirement and participate in the competition, the Government is making the solicitation and related unclassified documents available through SAM.gov. All unclassified solicitation and RFP materials associated with HRM II are available with this posting. 2. This amendment incorporates the Attachment 16 Supplemental Section 4 � Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors revision 2, dated 2026108, to reflect language updates. 3. This amendment reopens the question period. The question-and-answer period is hereby reopened. Interested vendors may submit questions no later than: 15 October 2026, 3:00 PM Eastern Time Questions shall be submitted by email to both Points of Contact: - Contracting Officer: Haydee.L.SotoCarreras@nga.mil - Contract Specialist: Adrianne.M.Crutchfield@nga.mil Questions already submitted through the ARC have already been accepted and shall not be resubmitted. Proposal submission instructions remain unchanged unless revised by a future amendment. 5. The Government anticipates addressing responses to vendor questions and any revisions to proposal submission procedures, including any extension to the proposal due date, through a subsequent amendment, if applicable. ***Amendment 0001 Clarification to SAM.gov Notice � RFP HM047626R0018, NGA Human Resource Management II (HRM II)*** *** This notice amendment provides clarification regarding access to solicitation HM047626R0018 and submission of questions and proposals *** 1.Solicitation Access: The RFP, RFP amendment 0001, all attachments, and the Contractor Bidder Library (CBL) will be available only through the classified Acquisition Research Center (ARC). The solicitation materials will not be posted or otherwise distributed through SAM.gov. 2. Classified ARC Access Instructions: All interested offerors are strongly encouraged to thoroughly review the access instructions provided in the SAM.gov RFP notice on September 23, 2026, and below, before attempting to access the Classified ARC. Offerors are responsible for ensuring they have the required access and for resolving any account or technical issues with the Classified ARC Technical Support Help Desk. L’ensemble des lots organisés par le présent marché visent à l’élaboration, la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement, la livraison, l’intégration avec support technique dans la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP ainsi que la maintenance de trois modules de formation/apprentissage au format e-learning, disponibles simultanément en versions française et néerlandaise. Les lots 1, 2 et 3 visent l’élaboration de trois programmes d’apprentissage (objectifs, contenus, dispositif pédagogique) rendus disponibles en langue française et destinés à s’intégrer dans des modules en e-learning. Ces 3 programmes portent sur les trois thématiques suivantes : - « Introduction aux achats publics des administrations communales et des CPAS bruxellois ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des administrations communales bruxelloises ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des CPAS bruxellois ». Les lots 4 et 5 visent la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement technique et la maintenance des trois modules de formation au format e-learning sur base des trois programmes d’apprentissage susmentionnés. Hébergement des modules e-learning : les modules de formation e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP (voir description technique en annexe). Le cas échéant, les modules e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS d’un ou plusieurs administrations clientes ou sur un site Internet. Il est à noter que le présent marché ne couvre pas les services liés à l’intégration des modules e-learning sur d’autres plateformes que celle mise à disposition par l’ERAP. Durée des modules e-learning : Les modules de formation au format e-learning visés par les lots 4 et 5 ont une durée respective estimée à 60 minutes (2 x 30 min. ou 4 x 15 min.). Thématique des modules : Ces modules s’intègrent dans un parcours de formation plus large destiné à l’onboarding des agents de niveau A, B ou C des administrations communales et des CPAS de la Région de Bruxelles-capitale. Estimation du nombre d’utilisateurs finaux pour chacun des trois modules d’apprentissage : environ 550 personnes par an (500 apprenants/utilisateurs finaux et 50 responsables représentants les administrations concernées + personnel ERAP). Durée du marché : pour tous les lots, le marché est conclu pour une durée d’un an, renouvelable trois fois pour la même durée, pour une durée totale de 4 ans (voir point II.7 pour les détails). Le marché est divisé en lots de la manière suivante : (1) LOT 1 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (2) LOT 2 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES BRUXELLOISES. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (3) LOT 3 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (4) LOT 4 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DU MODULE E-LEARNING D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES COMMUNES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS (DURÉE ESTIMÉE : 60 MINUTES), EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. (5) LOT 5 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DES DEUX MODULES D’APPRENTISSAGE EN E-LEARNING (CHACUN D’UNE DURÉE ESTIMÉE DE 60 MINUTES) PORTANT RESPECTIVEMENT SUR (1) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES COMMUNES BRUXELLOISES (2) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS, EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. Délais de livraison : Pour les lots 1, 2 et 3 (voir point III.2.6) ; Pour les lots 4 et 5 (voir point III.3.7)

Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction Project NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000003, located in Dutchess, Nassau, Suffolk and Saratoga Counties, New York; Sullivan County, New Hampshire; and Hampden County, Massachusetts. The project consists of bridge maintenance and pavement preservation of roadways and parking areas across several parks including Home of FDR National Historic Site (HOFR), Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (ELRO), Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site (VAMA), Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS), Saint Gaudens National Historic Park (SAGA), Sagamore Hill National Historic Park (SAHI), Saratoga National Historical Park (SARA) and Springfield Armory National Historical Park (SPAR). The work includes thin lift asphalt overlay, chip seal, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, pavement markings, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 29, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

title: Poland – System and support services – Usługa asysty technicznej narzędzia CMS wraz z jego rozbudową
description: 1. Przedmiotem zamówienia jest Usługa asysty technicznej narzędzia CMS wraz z jego rozbudową. Zamówienie obejmuje następujące działania: 1) Działanie I – obejmuje świadczenie asysty technicznej posiadanego przez Zamawiającego CMS polegające na: a) Usuwaniu błędów zaistniałych w CMS posiadanym przez Zamawiającego wraz z jego wszystkimi funkcjonalnościami, w tym poprawną integracją z posiadanym przez Zamawiającego systemem WOWZA Streaming Engine. Zapewnienie stabilności, bezpieczeństwa, spójności rozwiązania dla sześciu (6) instancji CMS (objętych asystą). b) Wsparciu pracowników Zamawiającego w zakresie obsługi i działania posiadanego CMS oraz istniejących serwisów (maksymalnie 50 zapytań / miesiąc dla wszystkich istniejących instancji objętych asystą oraz serwisów). 2) Działanie II (z Prawem opcji) – obejmuje rozbudowę i modyfikację CMS oraz istniejących serwisów opartych na narzędziu CMS (modyfikacja funkcjonalności, nowe funkcjonalności) w ramach roboczogodzin programistycznych: a) Zamawiający przewiduje w ramach Działania II maksymalnie 350 roboczogodzin, w tym: - 110 roboczogodzin jako zamówienie podstawowe, - 240 roboczogodzin jako zamówienie opcjonalne, w całym okresie trwania Umowy z tym, że jest to wartość maksymalna i z zastrzeżeniem lit. b. b) Zamawiający zastrzega sobie Prawo Opcji do Działania II. Zamawiający wskazuje, że z uwagi na okoliczności techniczne, organizacyjne roboczogodziny mogą zostać wykorzystane w mniejszym wymiarze, tj. w wymiarze zamówienia podstawowego czyli 110 roboczogodzin. W przypadku nie skorzystania przez Zamawiającego z prawa zlecenia rozbudowy i modyfikacji CMS w wymiarze większym niż 110 roboczogodzin, Wykonawca nie będzie wnosił żadnych roszczeń z tego tytułu. 2. Spełnianie wymogów WCAG na poziomie wymaganym zgodnie z obowiązującymi przepisami prawa (w tym m.in. Ustawy z dnia 4 kwietnia 2019 r. o dostępności cyfrowej stron internetowych i aplikacji mobilnych podmiotów publicznych, Rozporządzenia Rady Ministrów z dnia 12 kwietnia 2012 r. w sprawie Krajowych Ram Interoperacyjności, minimalnych wymagań dla rejestrów publicznych i wymiany informacji w postaci elektronicznej oraz minimalnych wymagań dla systemów teleinformatycznych, Ustawy z dnia 19 lipca 2019 r. o zapewnianiu dostępności osobom ze szczególnymi potrzebami). 3. Ze względu na specyfikę przedmiotu zamówienia Zamawiający przewiduje obowiązek dokonania przez Wykonawcę sprawdzenia dokumentów niezbędnych do realizacji zamówienia, udostępnionych w siedzibie Zamawiającego, zgodnie z zapisami pkt VIII Opisu przedmiotu zamówienia (OPZ) stanowiącego Załącznik nr 3 do SWZ. Niedochowanie powyższego obowiązku będzie skutkować odrzuceniem oferty na podstawie art. 226 ust.1 pkt 18 ustawy Pzp. 4. Zamawiający uprawniony jest do skorzystania z prawa opcji, o którym mowa w art. 441 ust. 1 ustawy Pzp, na zasadach opisanych w paragrafie 2 i 6 załącznika nr 2 do SWZ -projektowanych postanowieniach umowy (PPU). 5. Opis przedmiotu zamówienia (w skrócie: OPZ) stanowi: Załącznik nr 3 do SWZ / Załącznik nr 1 do projektowanych postanowień umowy. 6. Projektowane postanowienia umowy w sprawie powyższego zamówienia publicznego, które zostaną wprowadzone do treści umowy znajdują się w Załączniku nr 2 do SWZ. 7. Instrukcje dla Wykonawcy znajdują się na Platformie pod adresem: https://slaskie.ezamawiajacy.pl/servlet/HomeServlet?MP_module=main&MP_action=publicFilesList&clientName=slaskie&USER_MENU_HOVER=publicFilesList

buyer: VZW Vlaams Centrum voor Agro- en Visserijmarketing
title: Belgium – Advertising and marketing services – European Potato Promotion Campaign
description: From 2020 to 2025, VLAM, CNIPT, Bord Bia and Europatat collaborated on the European fresh potato promotion campaign “Potatoes, prepare to be surprised – Europe’s favourite since 1536”. Building on this experience, the four organisations are joining forces for a new three-year information and promotion campaign, co-funded by the European Union. The new campaign offers an opportunity to develop a fresh and distinctive creative concept. While lessons from the previous campaign can serve as inspiration, we expect an original, new approach, without being bound by the branding, slogan or visual identity of the previous campaign. The new campaign wants to stimulate the consumption of fresh potatoes at EU level and more specifically in three countries, i.e. Belgium (Flanders), France and Ireland. Target group of the campaign is people between 25 and 44 years old The communication objective of the new campaign is to highlight the ease of use (convenience) and versatility of fresh potatoes (pleasure) and their place in a contemporary lifestyle and a healthy, balanced and sustainable diet. The campaign activities include a mix of promotional activities, some implemented in all target countries, others in 1 or more target countries. Common activities include the design of a common look & feel, website, social media template and video. Local activities include collaboration with influencers and creation of local social media posts and/or videos. Our target group will be reached via a multi-channel approach, with a focus on video and social media advertising in all countries. This approach will be extended with native advertising in Flanders and Ireland and PR activities in France.

Le titulaire du marché devra notamment assurer les prestations suivantes : - Le conseil en stratégie de communication ; - La conception et la création des campagnes de communication de marque, de saisons, de spectacles, dans et hors les murs, et d'offres promotionnelles ; - La conception des principes et guidelines éditoriales associés aux saisons et aux campagnes de communication ; - La conception graphique et digital de supports de communication : brochures, programmes, affiches, bâches, documents promotionnels et contenus numériques ; - La production, l'exécution et la déclinaison des supports de communication print et digitaux, dans leurs différents formats et adaptations ; - La coordination avec les différents intervenants et prestataires associés aux opérations de communication, notamment les prestataires d'impressions, de fabrication et d'achat d'espaces media

title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction, Project NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000004, located in Essex County, New Jersey; Pike, Wayne, and Lackawanna Counties, Pennsylvania; and the City of Baltimore, Maryland. The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). The work includes micro surfacing, thin lift asphalt overlay, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, milling and overlay, concrete repair, drainage repairs, speed bump replacement, concrete paver installation, pavement markings, minor bridge repairs, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $3,000,000 to $4,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 6, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Wallkill River National Wildlife Refuge, Project NJ-NY ERFO FW WARI 2019-1(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000005, located in Sussex County, New Jersey; and Orange County, New York. The project consists of repairs to the Winding Waters Trail, Liberty Loop Trail (NE), Liberty Loop Trail (SW), and Dagmar Dale Nature Trail. The work includes embankment repairs, trail reconstruction, culvert replacement, stream regrading, headwall and wingwall installation, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $3,000,000 to $5,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 12, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance
description: *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30th, 2026 as of 10:30am ET. This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en. Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/artificial-intelligence-ai-decision-making-process-visibility-traceability-and-compliance-governance Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) Funding Mechanism: Contract MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE: Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. Phase 2: • The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. • The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report). • Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: No travel required. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice. The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices. Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight. Details: Essential (mandatory) Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required. 2. Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization. 2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks). 2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms. 2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments. 3. Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements. 3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention. 4. Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities. 4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital, Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act. 4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user. 4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. The system must identify whether each artifact was provided by an authorised individual [Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)]. 4E. Provide measurable results and clearly distinguish between results when performing a compliance assessments to determine whether compliance is met, partially met, not

title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: ATR Plant Protection System (PPS) Seismic Switch Replacement
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the management and operating contractor for the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified suppliers capable of providing environmentally and seismically qualified seismic switches for use in the Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) Plant Protection System (PPS). The purpose of this EOI is to identify suppliers with the technical capability, quality assurance program, testing facilities, and experience necessary to provide safety-related seismic switch equipment qualified for nuclear applications. This EOI is being issued for market research and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to identify potential suppliers for a future procurement opportunity. The EOI process is used by INL to develop a list of qualified and interested vendors that may be considered for future solicitations. BACKGROUND The ATR Plant Protection System currently utilizes seismic switches to provide a critical reactor protection function. Seismic switches detect ground motion and initiate a reactor scram when predetermined seismic thresholds are exceeded. The existing Kinemetrics Model TS-3A seismic switches are obsolete and have demonstrated performance degradation, resulting in increased reliance on limited spare inventory. Additionally, one seismic switch is currently out of service, placing the PPS in a reduced logic configuration. Replacement with modern, supported equipment is required to restore normal system configuration and ensure long-term reliability and maintainability. SCOPE OF INTEREST BEA seeks information from suppliers capable of providing complete seismic switch solutions meeting the functional, environmental, seismic qualification, testing, documentation, and quality assurance requirements typically associated with nuclear safety-related applications. Functional Capability Three-axis ground motion sensing capability. Dry contact output suitable for reactor protection system input. Adjustable seismic trip setpoints. Response times consistent with nuclear protection system applications. Long-term reliability and maintainability. In-situ testing and calibration capabilities. Environmental and Seismic Qualification Respondents should be capable of qualifying equipment consistent with applicable industry standards, including IEEE 603 IEEE 323 IEEE 344 ANSI/ISA-67.04.01 ASME NQA-1 Deliverables Suppliers should be capable of providing: Complete seismic switch assemblies. Required mounting hardware and accessories. Qualification documentation and test reports. Operation and maintenance manuals. Installation and interface documentation. Calibration and surveillance procedures. Certificates of conformance and applicable certifications. MINIMUM MANDATORY CAPABILITIES To facilitate evaluation, respondents should clearly identify whether they can meet the following minimum capabilities: Provide a seismic switch solution capable of detecting low-level seismic events suitable for reactor protection applications. Demonstrate environmental and seismic qualification in accordance with IEEE 323 and IEEE 344 methodologies. Maintain a Quality Assurance Program consistent with ASME NQA-1 requirements or equivalent controls. Support a qualified service life suitable for long-term nuclear facility operation. Provide qualification reports, testing documentation, calibration information, and supporting quality records. Provide long-term product support, maintenance recommendations, and obsolescence management. RESPONSE FORMAT AND SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested organizations shall submit a concise response demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities, and interest in supporting this requirement. Responses should be limited to approximately 10 pages, excluding product literature, drawings, certifications, and supporting quality documentation. Responses should include, at a minimum: Organization name, mailing address, and primary point of contact UEI and CAGE Code (if applicable) Business size and socio-economic classifications Technical capabilities Relevant experience Quality Assurance Program information Manufacturing and delivery capabilities Estimated lead times Assumptions, exceptions, or recommendations related to the requirement Responses shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to: Chase Egbert & Stacey Hill Email: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov and Stacey.Hill@inl.gov Responses must be received no later than: April 23, 2026 PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents should clearly identify any proprietary or confidential information contained within their submission. DISCLAIMER This Expression of Interest (EOI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or commitment by BEA or INL to procure supplies or services. BEA reserves the right to use information received through this EOI to evaluate market capabilities, acquisition strategies, and potential supplier interest. Submission of an EOI response does not guarantee participation in any future solicitation and does not obligate BEA or INL to award a contract. BEA is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing or submitting responses to this EOI. Information obtained through this process may be used to assist in developing future procurement requirements and solicitation strategies

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND NEXT GENERATION DISTRIBUTED COMMAND AND CONTROL
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace.
